card.band: 8 h. Buckets: containers, text styles, lists/tables, tracked changes, offset mapping. A frontier agent finishes the basics but misses nested spans and offset edge cases. A weaker model stops at plain-text extraction.
card.cheat: Stripping tags with a regex breaks the offset mapping that the hidden tests check. No upstream parser exists to copy.
card.grading: Hidden Rust tests through the public API on generated and sample ODF files, checking exact prose-span offsets and lint output. The existing cargo suite is a regression gate. Score is the fraction of cases passed.
card.reference: Our own implementation, about 1.2-1.8k lines including the zip/XML handling and offset mapping. It is validated against the hidden tests.
card.source: https://github.com/Automattic/harper issue #1427 @ head 37d344c (v2.13.0 release listed), Apache-2.0
card.task: Add an OpenDocument (.odt and flat .fodt) text parser to harper-core. It must extract prose spans with exact source offsets, skip code/metadata/tracked-change content and keep lint spans mapping back to the file. It needs a public Document constructor, a CLI input mode and offset-preserving suggestion application.
card.title: OpenDocument text parsing for the Harper grammar checker

spike_plan.kill_if: harper-core cannot build offline with the needed XML dependency; or the Document model cannot carry non-contiguous source offsets without rewriting the core; or hand-computed offsets cannot be reproduced for the nested-span and tracked-change cases within 60 minutes.
spike_plan.pass_if: Build succeeds offline or with vendored deps; extractor reproduces hand-computed offsets on all 5 generated files including nested spans and tracked-change skipping; lint spans map back to the file on one planted error; output is deterministic across 3 runs.
steps: Clone Automattic/harper at 37d344c into a throwaway container with network; check out and run cargo build -p harper-core and the existing test suite to get a real build time and status (smoke_build was not supplied).
Check whether an XML crate (quick-xml or similar) and zip are in the local cargo registry cache usable offline; if not, the card must ship vendored deps or drop the XML crate.

Write a throwaway ODT extractor: unzip content.xml with the existing zip crate, walk text:p, text:h, text:span, text:s, text:tab and text:line-break, and record a source-offset map for each prose character.
Generate 5 small .odt and .fodt files with known spans (nested spans, a list, a table cell, a tracked change, a code block) and check the offsets against hand-computed expected values.
Run harper-core's existing Document path on the extracted text and confirm lint spans map back to the file offsets for one planted error.
Re-run the extractor 3 times and confirm deterministic output.

v1.summary: The Harper repo and Apache-2.0 licence check out, and no public ODT parser or PR exists, but the cited issue #1427 is a LibreOffice-integration request that never mentions ODT, so the card needs a new paper trail (the ODF spec and the repo) before acceptance. The seed's smoke_build is empty, so build cost and offline XML-crate availability are unverified and must be settled in the spike before the card is accepted.

v2.note: The cited paper trail is contradicted: issue #1427 asks for LibreOffice/Linux app integration, not ODT/FODT parsing, and no PR or release note mentions OpenDocument. The feature and its exact-offset contract (offsets into what: zipped content.xml bytes or chars?) are our own design, so hidden tests risk rejecting other valid implementations. At about 1.5k lines it sits close to the DeepSWE single-feature calibration. Not built (smoke_build empty), and no XML crate is available offline.
